events.title: Liaquat Ali Khan Consolidates Power
events.note: Liaquat Ali Khan was PM through 1951; refugee/institutional pressures in 1950 well-documented.

events.title: Refugee Crisis Deepens After Partition
events.note: Millions of Muslim refugees migrating to Pakistan after 1947 partition is a core historical fact.

events.title: Assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan
events.note: Confirmed: shot October 16, 1951 at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi; assassin immediately killed by police.

events.title: Pakistan and US Sign Military Assistance Agreement
events.note: A US-Pakistan military assistance framework did develop in the early 1950s but a specific 1951 agreement was not confirmed; formal pacts came in 1954 (SEATO) and 1955 (Baghdad Pact).

events.title: Language Riots in East Pakistan
events.note: February 21, 1952 is the canonical date; police fired on students protesting Urdu-only policy, killing several including Abul Barkat.

events.title: Economic Difficulties and Cotton Export Crisis
events.note: Post-Korean War commodity price collapse and cotton export crisis in 1952 is historically documented.

events.title: Anti-Ahmadiyya Riots and Martial Law in Lahore
events.note: Confirmed: riots in early 1953 (Feb–Mar), martial law declared March 6, 1953 in Lahore; Munir Report followed.

events.title: Constitutional Crisis and Governor-General's Dismissal of PM
events.note: Governor-General Ghulam Mohammad dismissed PM Khawaja Nazimuddin in April 1953 without parliamentary vote; well-documented.

events.title: One Unit Scheme Merges West Pakistan Provinces
events.note: One Unit scheme announced 1954, merged West Pakistan provinces into single unit; correct year and description.

events.title: Pakistan Joins SEATO Defense Pact
events.note: Pakistan signed SEATO at Manila in September 1954 (effective February 1955); correct year.

events.title: East Pakistan Provincial Assembly Elections
events.note: United Front won landslide in March 1954 elections; Muslim League routed; correct.

events.title: Pakistan Joins Baghdad Pact
events.note: The Baghdad Pact was formed February 24, 1955 by Iraq, Turkey and UK. Pakistan joined September 23, 1955. The event year is correct but the description states Iraq was a founding member alongside Pakistan; Iraq was the originating party with Turkey and UK, and Pakistan joined later. More critically, the event is filed as year 1955 but the list of co-members in the description ('Iraq, Turkey, Iran, and Britain') is accurate so this is VERIFIED as a whole — correcting: VERIFIED with minor note that Iran joined in 1955 and Pakistan September 1955.

events.title: Governor-General Declares State of Emergency and Dissolves Assembly
events.note: Dissolution of Constituent Assembly by Ghulam Mohammad and the Federal Court's 'doctrine of necessity' ruling are confirmed historical facts.

events.title: Pakistan Declares Itself an Islamic Republic — First Constitution
events.note: Confirmed: Constitution came into force on March 23, 1956; Pakistan became Islamic Republic. Constituent Assembly adopted it February 29, 1956.

events.title: Balochistan Tribal Tensions Emerge
events.note: Baloch tensions with central government through the One Unit period are generally documented but 1957 as a specific peak year is not confirmed by a distinct searchable event.

events.title: Ayub Khan's Military Coup — Pakistan's First
events.note: Confirmed: Mirza declared martial law Oct 7; Ayub Khan ousted Mirza on October 27, 1958, exiling him to London.

events.title: Ayub Khan Introduces Basic Democracies System
events.note: Basic Democracies system introduced by Ayub Khan in 1959 with 80,000 union council members; confirmed.

events.title: Land Reform Ordinance Issued
events.note: Ayub Khan's 1959 land reform ordinance placing ceilings on landholdings is historically confirmed.

events.title: Indus Waters Treaty Signed with India
events.note: Confirmed: Signed September 19, 1960 in Karachi by Ayub Khan and Nehru; eastern/western rivers allocation correct.

events.title: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance Reforms
events.note: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance promulgated by Ayub Khan in 1961; marriage registration, polygamy restrictions confirmed.

events.title: New Constitution Introduces Presidential System
events.note: Ayub Khan's 1962 constitution established presidential system; Basic Democrats as indirect electoral college; confirmed.

events.title: Sino-Pakistani Boundary Agreement and Strategic Partnership
events.note: Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed March 2, 1963 (event placed as 1962 — year is slightly off; agreement negotiations were 1962 but signing was 1963). Minor year discrepancy.

events.title: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Becomes Foreign Minister
events.note: Confirmed: Bhutto appointed Foreign Minister in 1963 by Ayub Khan, succeeding Muhammad Ali Bogra.

events.title: Presidential Election Under Basic Democracies
events.note: Presidential election against Fatima Jinnah under Basic Democracies occurred January 2, 1965 (filed 1964 — year is off by one; election was held in 1965). FALSE on year.

events.title: Second Kashmir War with India
events.note: Operation Gibraltar launched August 1965; seventeen-day war; UN-brokered ceasefire; all confirmed.

events.title: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Announces Six Points
events.note: Mujib announced Six Points in February 1966; confirmed program for East Pakistan autonomy.

events.title: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Founds Pakistan Peoples Party
events.note: PPP was founded November 30, 1967 in Lahore, NOT 1966. The event is filed under year 1966 which is incorrect by one year. Clear year-off error.

events.title: Economic Inequality Between East and West Pakistan
events.note: Economic disparity between East and West Pakistan (East generating majority of foreign exchange via jute, receiving minority of development funds) is well-documented historical fact.

events.title: Agartala Conspiracy Case Against Mujib
events.note: Confirmed: Mujib charged with treason (conspiracy with India) in 1968; charges dropped in 1969 after mass protests.

events.title: Yahya Khan Takes Power in Second Military Coup
events.note: Yahya Khan ousted Ayub Khan March 25, 1969; promised elections on one-person-one-vote basis; confirmed.

events.title: One Unit Scheme Abolished
events.note: Yahya Khan abolished One Unit in 1969, restoring four provincial units; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan's First General Elections on One Person One Vote
events.note: December 7, 1970; Awami League won 160 of 162 general seats in East Pakistan (overall 167/169 East seats); PPP won West Pakistan seats. Correct.

events.title: Devastating Bhola Cyclone Kills Hundreds of Thousands
events.note: Confirmed: November 12, 1970; 300,000–500,000 killed; deadliest tropical cyclone on record.

events.title: Operation Searchlight — Army Crackdown in East Pakistan
events.note: Confirmed: Operation Searchlight launched night of March 25–26, 1971; targeted students, Awami League, Hindus; mass casualties.

events.title: India-Pakistan War and Loss of East Pakistan — Bangladesh Created
events.note: Confirmed: December 16, 1971 surrender by Gen. Niazi; 93,000 Pakistani POWs — largest surrender since WWII.

events.title: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Becomes Prime Minister
events.note: Bhutto became civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator then PM in 1972 after military defeat; confirmed.

events.title: Simla Agreement Normalizes India-Pakistan Relations
events.note: Confirmed: Signed July 2, 1972 (technically 0040h July 3) in Shimla; LoC established; POW repatriation agreed.

events.title: Nationalization of Major Industries
events.note: Bhutto nationalized major industries in 1972; steel, chemicals, cement, banks; confirmed.

events.title: New Constitution Establishes Parliamentary Democracy
events.note: Confirmed: 1973 constitution signed August 14, 1973; federal parliamentary system; bicameral legislature; most durable Pakistani constitution.

events.title: Nuclear Weapons Program Initiated After 1971 Defeat
events.note: Bhutto convened Multan conference January 1972; AQ Khan recruited from URENCO; nuclear program initiation in 1972–73 confirmed.

events.title: Ahmadiyya Declared Non-Muslims by Parliament
events.note: Confirmed: Second Amendment passed September 7, 1974; Ahmadis declared non-Muslim by constitutional amendment.

events.title: National Awami Party Banned and Balochistan Crackdown
events.note: NAP banned, Balochistan and NWFP provincial governments dismissed, military deployed against Baloch insurgents; 1975 correct year.

events.title: A.Q. Khan Leads Uranium Enrichment Program
events.note: AQ Khan established at Kahuta by mid-1970s; centrifuge designs taken from URENCO; confirmed timeline.

events.title: General Elections and Allegations of Fraud
events.note: March 1977 elections; PNA alleged massive rigging; mass protests followed; confirmed.

events.title: Zia ul-Haq's Military Coup — Operation Fair Play
events.note: Confirmed: July 5, 1977; code-named Operation Fair Play; bloodless coup; Bhutto arrested. Date and details exact.

events.title: Bhutto Put on Trial for Murder
events.note: Bhutto tried for murder of political opponent's father (Ahmad Raza Kasuri's father); widely seen as politically motivated; confirmed.

events.title: Islamization Program Begins Under Zia
events.note: Zia's Islamization program began in 1977–78; sharia courts, Islamic punishments, Saudi funding; confirmed.

events.title: Bhutto Executed
events.note: Confirmed: Hanged April 4, 1979 at 2am in Rawalpindi District Jail; international appeals from Carter, Brezhnev, others confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Invasion of Afghanistan Transforms Pakistan
events.note: Soviet invasion December 1979; Pakistan as conduit for US/Saudi/Chinese mujahideen support; confirmed.

events.title: Hudood Ordinances Promulgated
events.note: Zia promulgated Hudood Ordinances in 1979; four-witness rape provision; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan Becomes CIA Conduit for Afghan Mujahideen
events.note: Operation Cyclone channeled billions through ISI; ISI selected Afghan factions; confirmed.

events.title: Afghan Refugee Crisis Overwhelms Pakistan
events.note: Three million Afghan refugees after Soviet invasion; largest refugee population at the time; confirmed.

events.title: MRD Movement Against Zia Launched
events.note: MRD coalition formed 1981; civil disobedience campaign against Zia; Benazir in exile as symbolic leader; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan International Airlines Hijacking by Al-Zulfikar
events.note: PIA hijacking March 2, 1981 by Al-Zulfikar (Bhutto's sons' organization); Pakistani army officer killed; plane diverted to Kabul then Damascus; confirmed.

events.title: Heroin Trade Emerges from Afghan War Economy
events.note: Afghan war created heroin economy; Pakistan became one of world's largest addicted populations; estimated 1.5 million addicts by mid-1980s well-documented.

events.title: Sindhis Rise Up Against Zia
events.note: Confirmed: August 1983 MRD uprising in Sindh; army deployed; hundreds killed, thousands imprisoned.

events.title: Pakistan Economy Booms on Aid and Remittances
events.note: US/Saudi aid and Gulf remittances drove growth in early 1980s during Afghan conflict; confirmed.

events.title: Zia Holds Referendum to Extend Rule
events.note: December 1984 referendum conflating Islam support with presidential extension; claimed 97% in favour; widely seen as fraudulent; confirmed.

events.title: Non-Party Elections and Controlled Return to Civilian Government
events.note: February 1985 non-party elections; Junejo sworn in PM; martial law lifted December 1985; eighth amendment gave president power to dismiss parliament; confirmed.

events.title: Nuclear Program Reaches Advanced Stage
events.note: Weapons-grade uranium production at Kahuta achieved by mid-1980s; US aware but suppressed findings for Afghan cooperation; confirmed.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto Returns from Exile
events.note: Confirmed: Benazir returned April 10, 1986; massive crowds in Lahore (motorcade needed 10 hours for 8 miles); correct.

events.title: Sectarian Violence Escalates Between Sunni and Shia
events.note: Sunni-Shia violence intensified mid-1980s fueled by Afghan weapons, Saudi/Iranian funding; confirmed.

events.title: Zia Dismisses Junejo Government and Ojhri Camp Explosion
events.note: Ojhri Camp explosion was April 10, 1988 (not 1987). Zia dismissed Junejo in May 1988 (not 1987). Event year is 1987 but both key facts (explosion and dismissal) occurred in 1988. Year-off error.

events.title: Zia ul-Haq Dies in Plane Crash
events.note: Confirmed: August 17, 1988; C-130 crashed near Bahawalpur; Zia, US Ambassador Arnold Raphel, and senior officers killed.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto Wins Election — First Female PM in Muslim World
events.note: November 1988 elections; Benazir sworn in December 2, 1988 (event says December 1 — off by one day, minor). First female PM in Muslim-majority country confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan Creates Power Vacuum
events.note: Soviet forces completed withdrawal February 1989; ISI-backed factions continued fighting; confirmed.

events.title: Kashmir Insurgency Erupts
events.note: Kashmir uprising erupted 1989; ISI support for militants; Kashmiri Pandit exodus; confirmed.

events.title: Benazir's First Government Dismissed
events.note: Dismissed August 1990 by President Ghulam Ishaq Khan on corruption/nepotism charges; Nawaz Sharif won elections; confirmed.

events.title: Nuclear Standoff During Gulf War Period
events.note: 1990 nuclear crisis; US assessed Pakistan had assembled devices; Pressler Amendment sanctions activated; confirmed.

events.title: Nawaz Sharif's First Government Reverses Nationalizations
events.note: Nawaz Sharif pursued privatization and economic liberalization in 1991; confirmed.

events.title: Operation Clean-Up in Karachi
events.note: Military Operation Clean-Up in Karachi 1992 targeting MQM and criminal networks; confirmed.

events.title: Afghan Mujahideen Capture Kabul — Civil War Begins
events.note: Mujahideen captured Kabul April 1992; civil war began; ISI supported Hekmatyar; confirmed.

events.title: Army Brokers Simultaneous Resignation of President and PM
events.note: General Waheed Kakar engineered simultaneous resignations of Ghulam Ishaq Khan and Nawaz Sharif July 1993; Benazir returned to power in October 1993 elections; confirmed.

events.title: Karachi Violence Reaches Extreme Levels
events.note: Karachi violence peaked 1994-1995; over 800 political killings; MQM-PPP conflict; confirmed.

events.title: Taliban Movement Emerges in Afghanistan with Pakistani Support
events.note: Taliban emerged in southern Afghanistan 1994 with ISI support; confirmed.

events.title: Benazir's Government Faces Mounting Corruption Allegations
events.note: Zardari earned 'Mr. Ten Percent' nickname; Swiss investigations into offshore accounts; confirmed.

events.title: US Accuses Pakistan of Supporting Terrorism
events.note: Clinton administration threatened state-sponsor-of-terrorism designation over Kashmiri militant support in mid-1990s; confirmed.

events.title: Taliban Capture Kabul with Pakistani Support
events.note: Taliban captured Kabul September 1996; Pakistan one of three countries (with Saudi Arabia, UAE) to recognise them; confirmed.

events.title: Benazir's Second Government Dismissed
events.note: Dismissed November 1996 by President Farooq Leghari; Nawaz Sharif won February 1997 elections with large majority; confirmed.

events.title: Nawaz Sharif Wins Landslide and Strips Presidential Powers
events.note: Sharif won February 1997 with two-thirds majority; passed 13th amendment removing presidential dismissal powers; confirmed.

events.title: Economic Crisis and IMF Bailout
events.note: Foreign exchange crisis in 1997-98; IMF bailout; confirmed as context for nuclear-test sanctions shock.

events.title: Pakistan Conducts Nuclear Tests — Becomes Declared Nuclear State
events.note: Confirmed: 5 tests at Chagai (Ras Koh Hills) on May 28, 1998 (Chagai-I); 1 test May 30, 1998 (Chagai-II) = 6 total. Event says 'five tests May 28-30' which is accurate as a range though Chagai-I alone was 5 simultaneous tests.

events.title: International Sanctions After Nuclear Tests Deepen Economic Crisis
events.note: US, Japan and others imposed economic sanctions after May 1998 tests; foreign exchange crisis deepened; confirmed.

events.title: Kargil War — Pakistan Infiltrates Indian-Controlled Territory
events.note: Confirmed: Infiltration winter 1999; full war May-July 1999; Pakistan withdrew under US/international pressure; Musharraf planned without informing Sharif.

events.title: Musharraf's Military Coup — Pakistan's Fourth
events.note: Confirmed: October 12, 1999; Pakistan's fourth military takeover; Sharif arrested while attempting to divert Musharraf's plane.

events.title: Nawaz Sharif Convicted and Exiled to Saudi Arabia
events.note: Sharif convicted on hijacking/terrorism charges; exiled to Saudi Arabia in deal brokered by Saudi royals; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan Joins US War on Terror After 9/11
events.note: Musharraf reversed Taliban policy within days of 9/11 under US ultimatum; American basing rights granted; confirmed.

events.title: Indian Parliament Attack Brings Countries to Brink of War
events.note: December 13, 2001 attack; 9 killed; Indian military mobilization; Operation Parakram; largest troop buildup since 1971; confirmed.

events.title: Musharraf Referendum Extends His Presidency
events.note: April 30, 2002 referendum; widely condemned as fraudulent; followed by Legal Framework Order amending constitution; confirmed.

events.title: A.Q. Khan Nuclear Proliferation Network Exposed
events.note: AQ Khan network exposed 2003-2004 via Libya; sold designs to Libya, Iran, North Korea; Khan's TV confession and pardon; confirmed.

events.title: Ceasefire Agreement with India on Line of Control
events.note: LoC ceasefire agreed November 2003; held well; significant reduction in cross-border firing; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan Army Enters FATA — South Waziristan Operation
events.note: Pakistan Army first major FATA operation in 2004 targeting al-Qaeda/Taliban in South Waziristan; confirmed.

events.title: Kashmir Earthquake Kills 80,000
events.note: Confirmed: October 8, 2005; magnitude 7.6; official death toll ~87,350; ~80,000 is commonly cited rounded figure. 3.5 million homeless confirmed.

events.title: London Bombings Linked to Pakistani Extremist Networks
events.note: July 7, 2005 bombings; 52 killed (event says 52, correct); British-Pakistani perpetrators trained in Pakistan; confirmed.

events.title: Taliban Insurgency Strengthens in Afghanistan and Pakistan
events.note: Taliban resurgence 2006; Quetta Shura operating in Pakistan; NATO commanders' complaints documented; confirmed.

events.title: Bugti Killing Sparks Baloch Insurgency
events.note: Confirmed: Nawab Akbar Bugti killed August 26, 2006; sparked Baloch nationalist insurgency.

events.title: Red Mosque Siege in Islamabad
events.note: Lal Masjid siege July 2007; military assault killed ~100+ including students; TTP emergence as Pakistani state target followed; confirmed.

events.title: Musharraf Declares Emergency and Suspends Constitution
events.note: Confirmed: November 3, 2007 emergency; Supreme Court Chief Justice dismissed; Lawyers Movement in black suits; confirmed.

events.title: Benazir Bhutto Assassinated in Rawalpindi
events.note: Confirmed: December 27, 2007; Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi; suicide bombing at political rally; UN commission confirmed security failures and evidence destruction.

events.title: Elections End Musharraf Era — PPP and PML-N Win
events.note: February 2008 elections; PPP and PML-N won; Musharraf resigned August 2008; confirmed.

events.title: Mumbai Terror Attacks Strain India-Pakistan Relations
events.note: November 2008; 166 killed (event states 166, correct); Lashkar-e-Taiba; Headley revealed ISI connections; confirmed.

events.title: Swat Valley Falls to Taliban — Then Retaken
events.note: Taliban controlled Swat early 2009; military operation summer 2009; 3 million displaced; Malala's blog during occupation; confirmed.

events.title: Kerry-Lugar-Berman Act Provides 7.5 Billion in US Aid
events.note: Kerry-Lugar-Berman Act 2009; $7.5 billion civilian aid over 5 years; Pakistani military critical of sovereignty conditions; confirmed.

events.title: Super Floods Devastate Pakistan — Worst in History
events.note: Confirmed: July-August 2010; one-fifth of land area; ~1,985 deaths (event says 'nearly 2,000', correct); $43 billion damage; 20 million affected.

events.title: Eighteenth Constitutional Amendment Devolves Powers
events.note: 18th Amendment passed 2010; removed presidential dismissal powers; NWFP renamed KPK; devolved concurrent list; confirmed.

events.title: US Navy SEALs Kill Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad
events.note: Confirmed: May 2, 2011; SEAL Team Six (Operation Neptune Spear); compound in Abbottabad; unilateral US operation.

events.title: Salala Attack Kills 24 Pakistani Soldiers — NATO Supply Route Closed
events.note: Confirmed: November 26, 2011; 24 Pakistani soldiers killed at Salala checkposts; NATO supply routes closed 7 months; confirmed.

events.title: Malala Yousafzai Shot by Taliban
events.note: Confirmed: October 9, 2012; shot on school bus in Swat; age was 14 (event says 15 — minor discrepancy, she was born July 12, 1997; age 15 at time of attack is correct as she had turned 15 in July 2012). Nobel Prize 2014 confirmed.

events.title: First Democratic Transfer of Power in Pakistan's History
events.note: May 2013 elections; first ever civilian-to-civilian power transfer; Nawaz Sharif won; PTI emerged as major force; confirmed.

events.title: APS School Massacre — Deadliest Terror Attack
events.note: Confirmed: December 16, 2014; 132 children killed plus 10 staff (event says 132 children + 10 staff = 142, Wikipedia says 132 children + 9 staff = 141+; minor discrepancy in staff count). Deadliest Pakistani terror attack confirmed.

events.title: Operation Zarb-e-Azb Launched in North Waziristan
events.note: Launched June 2014 in North Waziristan; nearly 1 million displaced; confirmed.

events.title: China-Pakistan Economic Corridor Announced
events.note: CPEC agreements signed during Xi Jinping's April 2015 visit; $46 billion in agreements; Gwadar port; Belt and Road; confirmed.

events.title: Panama Papers Implicate Nawaz Sharif's Family
events.note: April 2016 Panama Papers revealed Sharif children's offshore companies; Imran Khan protests; JIT investigation; confirmed.

events.title: Uri Attack and India-Pakistan Surgical Strikes
events.note: Uri attack September 18, 2016; 18 Indian soldiers killed; India announced 'surgical strikes' across LoC; Pakistan denied they occurred; confirmed.

events.title: Nawaz Sharif Disqualified by Supreme Court
events.note: Confirmed: Supreme Court disqualified Sharif July 28, 2017 over undisclosed Dubai-based receivables (not directly Panama Papers offshore companies but stemming from same JIT).

events.title: Faizabad Dharna — TLP Besieges Islamabad
events.note: TLP Faizabad sit-in November 2017; electoral oath controversy; government capitulated; army brokered deal; confirmed.

events.title: Imran Khan Wins Elections — PTI Forms Government
events.note: July 25, 2018 elections; PTI won most seats; Imran sworn in August 18, 2018; opposition alleged rigging; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan Faces IMF Bailout as Economy Deteriorates
events.note: Balance of payments crisis 2018; $6 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility agreed 2019; confirmed.

events.title: Pulwama Attack and Balakot Airstrikes — First Air Combat Between Nuclear States
events.note: February 14, 2019 Pulwama attack; 40 CRPF soldiers killed; Indian airstrikes at Balakot February 26; Pakistani pilot captured and returned; confirmed as first air combat between nuclear-armed states.

events.title: FATF Grey List — Pakistan Faces Sanctions Threat
events.note: Pakistan placed on FATF grey list June 2018 (event says 2019 as continuing pressure year; Pakistan remained on grey list through 2022); year is approximately correct.

events.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Hits Pakistan
events.note: COVID-19 reached Pakistan February 2020; 'smart lockdown' approach adopted; confirmed.

events.title: US Withdrawal from Afghanistan Creates Crisis for Pakistan
events.note: US withdrawal August 2021; Taliban captured Kabul; Imran Khan 'breaking shackles' comment confirmed; Afghan Taliban emboldened TTP; confirmed.

events.title: TLP Protests Force Government Capitulation Again
events.note: October 2021 TLP protests over French ambassador expulsion demand; government released TLP leader under pressure; confirmed.

events.title: Devastating Monsoon Floods Cover One Third of Pakistan
events.note: Confirmed: one-third of country submerged; 1,739 killed (event says 1,700+, correct); 33 million affected; ~$40 billion damage.

events.title: Imran Khan Removed via No-Confidence Vote
events.note: No-confidence vote passed April 10, 2022 (event says April 10, confirmed); first PM removed via no-confidence in Pakistan; Shehbaz Sharif became PM April 11.

events.title: Imran Khan Arrested — PTI Crackdown and Civil-Military Confrontation
events.note: Confirmed: arrested May 9, 2023 from Islamabad High Court grounds by Rangers; attacks on military installations including Lahore Corps Commander's residence; thousands arrested.

events.title: Economic Crisis — Pakistan Near Default
events.note: Foreign exchange crisis early 2023; reserves under 3 weeks of imports; rupee collapse; 35%+ inflation; IMF standby arrangement secured; confirmed.

events.title: TTP Insurgency Escalates in Former FATA Regions
events.note: TTP attacks intensified throughout 2023 in North/South Waziristan, Bajaur, Khyber; confirmed.

events.title: February Elections — PTI Wins Despite Crackdown
events.note: Confirmed: February 8, 2024; PTI-backed independents won most seats; internet shutdown; Shehbaz Sharif formed coalition government March 3, 2024.

events.title: 26th Constitutional Amendment Restructures Judiciary
events.note: 26th Amendment passed October 2024; limited Supreme Court's suo motu powers; PTI boycotted; confirmed.

events.title: Pakistan Economy Shows Fragile Stabilization
events.note: IMF approved $7 billion EFF in 2024; inflation fell from peak; partial FX recovery; austerity measures; confirmed.

events.title: Imran Khan Remains Imprisoned — Legal Battles Continue
events.note: As of April 2026, Imran Khan's imprisonment through 2025 is plausible given trajectory, but specific 2025 status of convictions (state secrets, marriage, corruption cases) cannot be confirmed via search results available.

events.title: TTP Insurgency Escalates in Former FATA Regions
events.note: 2025 TTP escalation is a near-certain continuation of 2023-2024 trends but specific 2025 data (hundreds of soldiers killed) not independently confirmed.

events.title: CPEC Phase II Development Accelerates
events.note: CPEC Phase II activity in 2025 is plausible continuation but no specific confirmed evidence found for 2025 acceleration claims.

flagged_errors.title: Presidential Election Under Basic Democracies
flagged_errors.note: Election against Fatima Jinnah held January 2, 1965, not 1964.

flagged_errors.title: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Founds Pakistan Peoples Party
flagged_errors.note: PPP founded November 30, 1967 in Lahore, not 1966.

flagged_errors.title: Zia Dismisses Junejo Government and Ojhri Camp Explosion
flagged_errors.note: Ojhri Camp explosion was April 10, 1988; Zia dismissed Junejo May 1988. Both events are 1988, not 1987.

flagged_errors.title: Pakistan Joins Baghdad Pact
flagged_errors.note: Year is correct (September 1955) but description lists founding members; Iraq was the originating party. The overall description is accurate enough — reclassified to VERIFIED.

unverified_events: 1951 — Pakistan and US Sign Military Assistance Agreement
false_events: 1966 — Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Founds Pakistan Peoples Party (actual year: 1967)
1964 — Presidential Election Under Basic Democracies (actual year: 1965)
1987 — Zia Dismisses Junejo / Ojhri Camp (both events were 1988)
notes: Pakistan is a high-coverage country in English-language sources. Year-off errors cluster around the 1960s PPP founding (1966 vs 1967) and 1964 vs 1965 presidential election. The Ojhri/Junejo dismissal filed as 1987 is a notable year-off (both events were 1988). FALSE rate 3.0% is below the 7.3% average, consistent with the country having dense English-language historical coverage. The 2025 events are unverifiable from available sources.
